Why This Issue Is Happening (Root Cause)
This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.
1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes
When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):
• UI is rendered *by a Camera*
• It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*
• Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path
• On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:
Not render at all, or
Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)
This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.

2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency
When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.
In other words:
> Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*.
3. Why this happens only on some Android devices
Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes
Key Takeaway
The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:
> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*
Screen Space – Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.

Hey guys, I did not read the doc that [PERSON_NAME_0092] was going to be removing lives from HUD and Minigames hub, so I just did to start a branch.

I suggest we all work on a feature branch, and once the economy changes are completed we can move it to develop if need it.

Working branch is `EconomyChanges`

*Fresh way to jump into levels:* Lives are out, now you can enter using *1 Ticket* or *1,000 Coins*. Got a timed *Unlimited Ticket*? Play freely while it’s active.
*Cleaner, clearer UI:* The Play button now shows your *Tickets* (or *Unlimited* status), and the lives counter is removed. “Free entry” replaces infinite lives anywhere it used to appear.
*Quests and rewards revamped:* Lives-based quests and rewards are removed, and *Daily and Weekly Chests now grant Tickets* as part of progression.
*Rebalanced economy and challenge:* You’ll earn *more Coins* from levels, *character upgrades now cost Gems (not Coins)*, and streak perks plus assistance were tuned to keep wins feeling earned.

rec.body_text:
Economy Changes for Domino Delights
Our goal is to make the game net negative in terms of the game balance. To accomplish this we’ll make 5 major changes.
1- We are removing the 	 lives system and replacing it with tickets.
We need a ticket icon and an infinite ticket icon from Martin and BRIAN.
Ticket cost: 1 ticket = 1,000 coins (same as current hearts).
Level cost: Levels always cost 1,000 coins. We will not scale level cost over time like Domino Dreams.
The 1,000 coin cost is roughly half the price of most boosters, which feels aligned.
Core rule
 Playing a level always requires either:
Spending 1,000 coins, or
Using 1 ticket or
Having timed [USERNAME_54272]
Play button behavior (OWEN)
 We will have three versions of the play button:
Coins-only state (no tickets owned)
Play button visuals remain as they are today.
Under the button, show the cost: 1,000 with the coin icon.
Tapping the button spends 1,000 coins to start the level.
Ticket state (player has standard tickets)
